title: Microplastic SEM Sample Preparation
author: Melissa B Duhaime
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uy8exzw

steps.title: Rinse Microplastic Sample
steps.instruction: Remove loosely associated debris from the microplastic sample using a PBS bath.

substeps.instruction: Fill a petri dish with enough PBS to submerge the microplastic sample.
Rinse the plastic in the PBS bath.

steps.title: Dehydrate Samples
steps.instruction: Perform a series of dehydration washes using ethanol (ETOH) or HMDS.

substeps.instruction: Create baths of 25% ETOH, 50% ETOH, 70% ETOH, 95% ETOH, 100% ETOH, 100% ETOH, 2 ETOH, 1 ETOH: 1 HMDS, 1 HMDS, and 1 HMDS (as indicated).
Submerge each piece of plastic in each bath and incubate for 15 minutes per wash.

steps.title: Air-Dry Samples
steps.instruction: Air-dry the dehydrated samples overnight in a desiccator located underneath a fume hood (12:00:00).

steps.title: Mount and Secure Sample
steps.instruction: Affix the plastic sample to an aluminum stud and secure it with carbon paint.

substeps.instruction: Affix plastic to double-sided carbon tape on an aluminum stud.
Draw a strap of carbon paint from the stud base to the top of the plastic.

steps.title: Sputter-Coat Sample
steps.instruction: Sputter-coat the plastic sample with heavy metal.

steps.title: SEM Imaging
steps.instruction: Image the sample under a scanning electron microscope (SEM) as soon as possible following sputter-coating.

substeps.instruction: Note: Samples can be kept for a maximum of 2 weeks after preparation.
